findings.title: Quarantine rule can erase evidence of real model mutations
findings.location: Section 2, Seam B; Section 6, Glossary — Quarantine
findings.evidence: Seam B: "A call whose orchestrator-side timeout expires while COM execution is in progress is recorded as `TimedOut`, but the COM operation may still complete and mutate the model." Glossary: "A late message received after a terminal lifecycle state is logged and discarded; it never updates session state, never contributes to DHF..."
findings.problem: If a timed-out COM call later succeeds, the spec allows a real model mutation to occur while the late completion is discarded and excluded from DHF.
findings.why_it_matters: The audit trail can claim a timeout while omitting the mutation that actually happened, breaking replayability, recovery reasoning, and the stated regulatory-traceability framing.
findings.proposed_fix: Require post-timeout completions that may imply model mutation to be captured in DHF as a recovery/out-of-band event, or require the recovery step to record the resulting observed state delta before the next turn can proceed.

findings.title: Termination reason attribution is stronger than the stated detection mechanism
findings.evidence: "Ungraceful termination (add-in crash, SolidWorks exit, orchestrator kill, WebSocket disconnect) is detected via heartbeat absence; the resulting session closure records the termination reason."
findings.problem: Heartbeat absence can show liveness loss, but it cannot by itself distinguish add-in crash vs SolidWorks exit vs orchestrator kill vs network/WebSocket failure.
findings.why_it_matters: The system will record cause codes it cannot actually observe, producing false audit data and misleading operational diagnostics.
findings.proposed_fix: Reduce closure reasons to observable categories such as explicit shutdown, superseded session, and heartbeat-timeout/unknown disconnect, or specify the extra signals required to distinguish the listed causes.

findings.title: SPEC-04 has an unstated semantic dependency on SPEC-02
findings.location: Section 1, Module Map; Section 6, Glossary — AddinSessionId and DHF Session; Section 7, Build-Readiness
findings.evidence: Module Map: "SPEC-04 ... Depends On `SPEC-01 (message shapes only)`". Glossary: "AddinSessionId ... Derivation algorithm ... is specified in SPEC-02." Also: "DHF Session... Opens on first AddinReadyMessage for a given AddinSessionId. Closes when a different AddinSessionId arrives..." Section 7: "SPEC-02 + SPEC-04 converge in parallel (they don't touch each other)".
findings.problem: SPEC-04 session epoching, StateVersion reset behavior, and reconciliation semantics depend on how SPEC-02 generates and rotates AddinSessionId, so the stated dependency map is incomplete.
findings.why_it_matters: The claimed review order and isolation are unsound; SPEC-04 can drift from the identifier semantics it relies on.
findings.proposed_fix: Move the AddinSessionId semantic contract into SPEC-00 or SPEC-01, or explicitly declare SPEC-04 depends on SPEC-02 and update the dependency/review order text.

findings.title: Top-level descope policy conflicts with mandatory timeout recovery
findings.location: Section 3, Mandatory vs Stretch; Section 2, Seam B
findings.evidence: Section 3: "Descope priority (LIFO): ... error recovery ... all stretch." Seam B: "SPEC-03 defines a mandatory post-timeout recovery flow ... before subsequent turns may proceed."
findings.problem: The document marks error recovery as stretch, then requires recovery as a mandatory safety gate after timeouts.
findings.why_it_matters: A team following the descope list can remove behavior that the lifecycle contract requires to avoid corrupted or unknown model state.
findings.proposed_fix: Split recovery into mandatory safety-critical recovery and optional UX recovery, and mark the mandatory post-timeout path as never-descopable.

findings.title: Post-timeout recovery flow lacks deterministic selection and success criteria
findings.evidence: "mandatory post-timeout recovery flow (state refresh or undo-group rollback) before subsequent turns may proceed. Details in SPEC-03."
findings.problem: The contract names two recovery strategies but does not define when to use each one, who decides, or what observable condition proves recovery succeeded.
findings.why_it_matters: Different implementations can make incompatible choices and still claim compliance, leaving state divergence unresolved in the highest-risk path.
findings.proposed_fix: Add seam-level rules for recovery strategy selection and completion, including required checks before accepting the next turn.

findings.title: Architecture-test enforcement claim ignores runtime seam failures
findings.evidence: "Each seam is one-directional. Violations are detected by `NetArchTest` rules..." and "The full transport contract — including connection lifecycle, error semantics, reconnect behavior, and threading guarantees — is defined in SPEC-01."
findings.problem: NetArchTest can enforce compile-time reference boundaries, but it cannot detect runtime WebSocket behavior, cross-runtime serialization mismatches, reconnect semantics, or threading violations.
findings.why_it_matters: The document overclaims how seam compliance will be verified and leaves the riskiest integration behaviors without an explicit test mechanism.
findings.proposed_fix: Limit NetArchTest to compile-time dependency enforcement and add required contract/integration tests for transport, serialization, reconnect, and threading behavior.

findings.title: Turn completion boundary is undefined when a timeout triggers recovery
findings.location: Section 2, Seam C; Section 2, Seam B; Section 6, Glossary — Turn
findings.evidence: Seam C: "one DHF write per completed turn." Seam B: "mandatory post-timeout recovery flow ... before subsequent turns may proceed." Glossary: "one DHF entry per completed turn."
findings.problem: The contract does not define whether a timed-out execution turn is considered complete at timeout, after late-message quarantine, or only after recovery/rollback finishes.
findings.why_it_matters: DHF entry contents, hash-chain ordering, and replay semantics become implementation-defined in a core failure case.
findings.proposed_fix: Define the exact close point for timeout cases and whether recovery outcome is stored in the same turn entry, a follow-up entry, or a separate recovery event.
